findings.body:
**Recheck blackout at fixer launch, after worktree preparation.**

At 09:49, a 10-minute attempt fits before a 10:00 blackout. If retention and reset take two minutes, dispatch at `crq_repair.py:478` starts a new 10-minute window that ends at 10:01. Recheck immediately before the paid launch, including fallback launches after cleanup. If the attempt no longer fits, defer it without recording an unknown paid outcome.
findings.title: Recheck blackout at fixer launch, after worktree preparation.

findings.body:
**Check recovery conflicts before entering dry-run mode.**

With repair enabled, `--triage-dry-run --recover-job x` returns from `crq_repair.py:1237–1243` before the conflict check. The caller gets exit code 0 instead of a usage refusal. Move mode validation before the dry-run branch. Keep a standalone dry run unchanged.
findings.title: Check recovery conflicts before entering dry-run mode.

findings.body:
**Protect child registration from interruption after `fork()`.**

If the parent receives `KeyboardInterrupt` after `crq_repair.py:961` but before it records the PID at Line 1001, the child can pass its gate while the parent's `finally` has no record of it. The coordinator can return without reaping that child. Make the parent-side fork-to-registration transition interrupt-safe. Keep the existing behavior of waiting for registered children rather than killing them.

Based on learnings, “`drain_items` must reap admitted forked workers before returning and releasing service.lock, including when admission is interrupted; it must not kill paid workers during cleanup.”
findings.title: Protect child registration from interruption after `fork()`.

findings.body:
**Reject an empty `--job` selector instead of draining the inbox.**

With repair enabled, `--job=` produces an empty string. The truthiness check at `crq_repair.py:1248` treats it as absent, so the invocation reaches `drain(config)` and can launch unrelated paid jobs. Use option presence to select the mode. Then require all three values to be nonempty before selecting a job. Preserve automatic drain only when no selector was supplied.
findings.title: Reject an empty `--job` selector instead of draining the inbox.

findings.body:
**Keep a malformed result from blocking every item in the drain.**

If a current queued job has `{broken` in `result.json`, `pending()` raises during priority sorting at `crq_repair.py:853`. The item-level exception handler has not been entered, so no item runs. Handle an unreadable or malformed result per job at both admission call sites. Preserve the artifact for harvest and continue with other items. Do not treat the malformed result as permission to rerun the fixer.
findings.title: Keep a malformed result from blocking every item in the drain.

findings.body:
**Emit one JSON document when an automatic drain runs triage.**

`crq_repair.py:799` writes the triage report. The same invocation then writes `{"status":"drained"}` through `main`. A caller that parses stdout as one JSON document rejects the output. Return the triage report to `run` and let `main` write once. Include the report in the drain result and return it directly for a configured dry run.

As per coding guidelines, “stdout is still exactly one JSON artifact.”
findings.title: Emit one JSON document when an automatic drain runs triage.

findings.body:
**Serialize operational failures at the CLI boundary.**

A complete selector with the wrong finding digest raises from `select_job` at `crq_repair.py:1298`. The exception escapes `main`, so an automated caller receives no JSON result. Convert operational exceptions to a JSON error with exit code 1. Keep usage errors on exit code 2 and normal skip results on exit code 0.

As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout” and exit code 1 denotes a thrown error.
findings.title: Serialize operational failures at the CLI boundary.

findings.body:
**Return a JSON usage error when argument parsing fails.**

At `crq_repair.py:1225`, `--job` without a value makes `argparse` exit with code 2 before `main` writes anything to stdout. Route parser errors through the CLI result writer and retain exit code 2. Test the exit code and stdout together. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/argparse.html?utm_source=openai))

As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout.”
findings.title: Return a JSON usage error when argument parsing fails.

findings.body:
**Keep a rate-limited provider out of the ready set during the global pause.**

With `fallback_models` set, `dispatch_paused` returns `None` when any ready role's provider has no unexpired cooldown entry. A missing entry reads as `''`, which compares as expired (`crq_repair.py:270-273`). The Codex fixer's provider is in that set. `fallback_roles` includes the original role first (`189-192`), and `provider_ready` returns true for providers outside its key map (`195-199`). A Codex `rate-limit` stop writes the global pause (`418-421`, `490-493`, `96-111`), but it never records a provider cooldown. The non-CQ branch of `dispatch` returns `_dispatch` directly (`277-280`). The next item then passes the check at `1085-1086` and can launch Codex during a pause that the code says must block all model calls (`1086`, `420`).

Required behavior: a provider that returned a `rate-limit` stop must not count as ready until its retry time. Choose the mechanism. Either record that provider's cooldown on the non-CQ path, or stop the override at `272-273` from treating an unrecorded provider as available. The trigger is any ready role, not only a CQ judge.
findings.title: Keep a rate-limited provider out of the ready set during the global pause.

findings.body:
**Apply the recorded-checkout guard to deferred mechanical verification.**

The mismatch guard at `apps/crq-python/crq_repair.py:389-390` checks only `pending_judge`. If a deferred `pending_mechanical` candidate loses its recorded checkout, `resume_worktree` falls back to the original checkout (`crq_repair.py:358-362`). The `pending_mechanical` branch then calls `mechanical` on that checkout (`crq_repair.py:451-452`). `verify` rejects the candidate because its commits are not ancestors of the original `HEAD` (`crq_repair/__init__.py:72-73`). The generic handler then drops `pending_mechanical`, records a mechanical failure on the A2 attempt, and advances the rung (`crq_repair.py:600-643`). The candidate is never detector-verified, so a valid repair can be lost. The guard must also cover `pending_mechanical`, as the judge path already does.

Apply the same fail-closed handling to both deferred states:

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-    if (result.get('pending_judge') and result.get('worktree')
+    if ((result.get('pending_judge') or result.get('pending_mechanical')) and result.get('worktree')
             and Path(result['worktree']).resolve() != Path(wt).resolve()):
-        # The A2 tree the deferred judge must inspect is gone: judging the
-        # base tree would record a verdict and snapshot for the wrong checkout.
+        # The recorded candidate tree is gone: verifying or judging the base
+        # tree would record a result for the wrong checkout.
         result.update(verdict='FAILED',
                       reason='pending judge worktree unavailable; needs human',
                       finished_at=utc())
         result.pop('pending_judge', None)
+        result.pop('pending_mechanical', None)
         atomic(result_path, result)
         return result
```

</details>

The `reason` text is shared with the judge path. Keep it unchanged or update it, but do not let it name only the judge.
findings.title: Apply the recorded-checkout guard to deferred mechanical verification.
